english.title: Publish an advertisement likely to lead to the use of a prescription only medicine
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) published an advertisement that was likely to lead to the use of a prescription only medicine
english.legislation: Contrary to regulations 284(1) and 303(1) and (3) of the Human Medicines Regulations 2012.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: (i) This offence does not apply to an advertisement which is part of a vaccination campaign relating to a medicinal product that is a vaccine or serum and has been approved by the Ministers - see regulation 292.(ii) The offence also does not apply in relation to campaigns relating to suspected or confirmed spread of pathogenic agents, as per regulation 291A.

other.penalty:
Summary: A fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: Two years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
